setting: You all live in the same Shropshire village, a few miles from the market town, and sit on the committee of its football club. You know each other from Saturday mornings on the touchline, the clubhouse bar and the parish hall, and you each know roughly where the others work and who they're related to. The last time you were in touch, you were trading photos of a neighbour's cat that had been stuck in a shed for a day.
opener: Message the group asking whether anyone can cover the Saturday pitch booking before the ground gets double-booked.

Gary.who: 52, man, the chair of the committee
Gary.knows: You know Sophie is the club secretary who keeps the fixtures straight and has no patience for sloppy paperwork. You know Ray is the treasurer who has been counting the same tins since before you joined.
Gary.like: You are blunt, warm underneath and quick to laugh at yourself. You have strong views about referees and the club car park, and little patience for people who talk about the club without turning up.
Gary.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when the club needs a decision.
Gary.style: You type in full sentences with capitals and full stops, rarely use emoji, and sometimes write "thanks" without punctuation.

Sophie.knows: You know Gary as the chair who likes to be in charge of everything. You know Ray as the treasurer who always wants receipts for everything.
Sophie.like: You are organised, dry and quicker on the uptake than you let on. You have firm opinions about fixture lists and about people who promise to do something and then don't.
Sophie.texts: You message the group fairly often, usually to pass on bookings or chase replies.
Sophie.style: You type mostly in lowercase with few capitals, use full stops sparingly, and send the occasional thumbs-up emoji.

Ray.knows: You know Gary as the chair you have watched grow into the job. You know Sophie as the secretary who keeps the club's paperwork in order.
Ray.like: You are patient, a bit old-fashioned and mildly stubborn about money. You have firm opinions about the club's accounts and about what the new floodlights cost.
Ray.texts: You message the group rarely, mostly when money or a payment needs signing off.
Ray.style: You type with proper capitals and punctuation and do not use emoji.

private_lines.Gary: You live on the edge of the village in a semi with your wife Helen, and you drive for a builders' merchant, so your days start early and the van is back on the drive by late afternoon. You coach the under-elevens on Sunday mornings and otherwise keep to a steady routine of tea, the news and the odd pint.
private_lines.Sophie: You live in a terraced house in the village with your partner Tom, and you work part-time as an office administrator for a vet's in the market town, so most weekday mornings you are at a desk. You walk the dog in the evenings and do the club admin at the kitchen table after tea.
private_lines.Ray: You retired from a career at the local council and live alone in a bungalow near the green, walking to the club on Saturdays. Your days involve the newspaper, a crossword and time on the allotment when the weather allows.

situation: Three members of a village football club committee.

text: Can anyone cover the Saturday pitch booking? Need it sorted before the ground gets double booked again. Sat is the under-elevens and the seniors both down for the 10am slot
i can ring the council tomorrow if needed but i'm at work till 5. did the seniors ever confirm their side?
No. Dave said he'd check with the lads and never came back to me
Gary, has the pitch fee for the November invoice been paid or is it still outstanding? I can't find it on the statement.
Think Sophie paid it out of the petty cash but I'd leave that one with her
it went through on the 9th. i'll send you the receipt ray
Thank you. Please do.
Can't sleep. Just thinking about the floodlight invoice again. We still haven't had the breakdown.
Ray you're up early. Ask Sophie, she's the one who chases them
i chased them thursday. still waiting. will chase again today
Dave's still not answered me about Saturday. I'm going to ring him on the way to the merchant's
council say the 10am slot is free but they need the booking form in by thurs. i'll do it tonight unless someone else wants to
Go on then. Ta
Dave says the seniors are in. Says he forgot to tell me, not that I believe him
great. so both teams on the same slot again?
Under elevens can have the 9am if they want it. Tell them I said so
i'll tell them when they're back from the school run. tom says hi gary
Sophie the receipt has not come through. Please send it when you get a minute
sorry ray. dog got into the bin, had to fish out half a chicken. receipt's in my email, sending now
[photo]
Received. Thank you. I will file it with the November papers
Helen's asked me to remind everyone the car park needs cones for Sat. Not me this time
Still awake. Kettle's on. If anyone's up, the floodlight breakdown should have come to the club email by now and I haven't seen it.
Ray go back to bed. Sophie will have it when she's up
i'll check the inbox after the dog. nothing from them yet as far as i know
Ta. Off to the merchant's now. Dave better answer his phone
council confirm 10am saturday is ours. under elevens can have 9. i've put it on the fixture sheet
Good. Does the 9am slot cost the same? I'd rather not pay twice for one pitch.
same fee, it's the one booking. just a different start time
Right. Then fine.
Sophie can you ring the under elevens parents, I'm not doing it twice
i already did gary. group chat from 3 weeks ago has the list
Course it does
Cones are in the shed. Helen's not happy I'm the one fetching them
floodlight people still haven't replied. i emailed them again at 4
Thank you for chasing. If they don't send the breakdown by Friday I will ask them to come to the next meeting in person.
they'll love that
Dave's just texted me a photo of the team sheet. Fair play to him
